title: Three rules: define risk, size on max loss, keep dry powder
summary: After almost 25 years trading derivatives, the speaker keeps three rules. Define the risk on every trade: no one-by-two call spreads and no short straddles. Size each trade on its maximum possible loss, not on premium targets; even in the core portfolio no single name exceeds 5%. Keep dry powder so you can act in a crash instead of facing margin calls.

steps.caption: The core portfolio. Rule two: no more than 5% in any single name.
The options sleeve holds only defined-risk trades. Rule one: no short tail risk such as short straddles.
Size every trade on its maximum possible loss, not on how much premium you want each week.
Rule three: dry powder. Cash lets you buy in a crash instead of facing margin calls.
A forced liquidation in a crash wastes the best opportunities. Cash keeps them open.

takeaways: Define the risk on every trade. Avoid structures with short tail risk.
Size trades on the maximum possible loss, with no single name above 5%.
Keep dry powder so a crash is an opportunity, not a margin call.
caveats: The 25-year track record is the speaker's own claim. Part of the transcript is missing.
